title: import and migrate should honour --render too
findings_note: the two bulk-load holdouts from S45/S47

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
S45 added `--render` to the nine item-mutating commands and S47 to the prose ones, but
`import` and `migrate` — the two bulk-load paths — were left out. They mutate the most
(a whole roadmap at once) and both end by telling you to run `slicer render`, so they are
exactly where the flag would help. Folding them in makes `--render` a universal
convention across every command that writes state.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - `src/slicer/cli.py` — the `import` and `migrate` registrations, and the `_mutating` guard

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `import FILE --render` leaves `check` clean with no separate render.
2. `migrate --from DIR --render` does the same.
3. `import FILE --dry-run --render` renders nothing (a dry run changed nothing, and may
   have no project to load).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Wrap `cmd_import` and `cmd_migrate` with the existing `_mutating` helper and add `--render`
via `_render_flag`. Teach `_mutating` to skip rendering when `--dry-run` is set: a dry run
writes nothing, and for `migrate` into an empty directory there is no project to reload, so
rendering then would fail rather than no-op.

**Not in this slice:** rendering by default without the flag; the flag stays opt-in,
consistent with every other command.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `slicer import roadmap.md --render && slicer check` is clean.
